pages.title: Architecture
pages.summary: How Clio Coder composes its entry points, domain modules, tool surface, and worker runtime into a single coding agent process, and the static import rules that keep those layers decoupled.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces
pages.summary: The argument-parsing and subcommand-dispatch entry point for every Clio Coder CLI surface, the configure wizard and target-selection flows, the headless main-agent runner, and the fleet authoring/execution and read-only run-viewer commands.

pages.title: Core: settings schema, layered configuration, bus contracts, safe exec, and session routing
pages.summary: The shared foundation modules under src/core that every domain depends on: the one strict settings schema and its layered merge, the event-bus channel registry with payload contracts, the sandboxed subprocess runner, the session-local routing state machine, and the workspace file enumerator.

pages.title: Domains agents
pages.summary: The agents domain loads and validates worker recipes, normalizes their specs, and exposes a catalog for dispatch, plus the typed result contracts and fleet-contract machinery that bound what each worker may claim and change.

pages.title: Config Domain
pages.summary: The config domain owns the single strict startup settings snapshot, watches settings files for changes, classifies each changed leaf into a hot-reload / next-turn / restart-required bucket, and dispatches bus events so other domains can observe the new value without importing the config internals.

pages.title: Context Domain
pages.summary: The context domain owns project handbook management, codewiki indexing, wiki generation, external agent-rule adoption, and the working-set eviction policies that control what the model sees on each request.

pages.title: Dispatch domain
pages.summary: How Clio resolves, admits, executes, and finalizes worker runs: the dispatch bundle's contract, routing decisions, fleet execution, and gate-decision persistence.

pages.title: Domains evidence
pages.summary: How Clio builds and reads forensic evidence bundles: the fixed eight-file layout, the canonical five-axis trust model, provenance admission, export-boundary redaction, and the CLI, tool, and observability entry points.

pages.title: Domains extensions
pages.summary: The harness extension contract: extensions declare command tools and hook declarations in a strict manifest, the operator runtime forks a private child process to inject the API, and a generation-stamped snapshot system pairs extension packages with middleware hooks so no reader sees state from two generations. Compatibility and integrity checks gate every package before it can run.

pages.title: Domains gateway
pages.summary: The MCP gateway: JSON-RPC 2.0 framing over stdio, the one-process client that spawns and manages MCP servers, the trust model for project-declared servers, and the metadata cache for tool catalogs.

pages.title: Domains interop
pages.summary: How Clio detects installed coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Antigravity and others), projects their resources into portable Clio packages, and wires them as ACP delegation peers behind an explicit consent record.

pages.title: Domains lifecycle
pages.summary: Diagnose an install with `clio-coder doctor`, migrate versioned state through `runPending`, and detect the install method so an upgrade never offers npm-global reinstall to a source checkout.

pages.title: Domains memory
pages.summary: Session-scoped task memory bank for background intervention, durable approved memory store for cross-session retrieval, and the promotion bridge between them.

pages.title: Middleware Domain
pages.summary: The unified hook-based effect layer that observes five lifecycle events (before_tool, after_tool, turn_start, turn_end, on_compaction), evaluates ordered registrations, and emits effects that steer tool admission, reminders, continuations, and operator notices.

pages.title: Domains mux
pages.summary: The pane multiplexing layer: the herdr socket client, dock controller for managed panes, Yazi file-manager integration, protocol floors, and the ownership rule that confines every mutating call to panes Clio created.

pages.title: Domains observability
pages.summary: The observability domain folds dispatch bus events, session cost tracking, and forensic evidence builds into a single bounded snapshot consumed by product surfaces. It owns the live projection, the SQLite trace mirror, the cost tracker, and the out-of-turn usage ledger.

pages.title: Domains plugins
pages.summary: How plugins are discovered, verified against recorded digests, installed into user or project scopes, and projected as resource roots for skills, prompts, agents, and fleets.

pages.title: Prompt Compiler
pages.summary: How prompt fragments are loaded from disk, compiled into a stable system prompt, and cached for prefix reuse.

pages.title: Domains providers
pages.summary: How Clio registers runtimes, probes targets, merges model capabilities, resolves runtime targets with context-window and thinking diagnostics, and stores credentials safely.

pages.title: Domains quota
pages.summary: How Clio reads Anthropic, Codex, and Antigravity subscription usage into shared snapshots, caches them with a 5-minute TTL instead of a background timer, and feeds the footer, welcome banner, and usage overlay.

pages.title: Domains resources
pages.summary: How Clio discovers, loads, and validates skills, prompt templates, and library packages, and the plan/apply/verify lifecycle that installs and removes them.

pages.title: Domains safety
pages.summary: The safety domain classifies tool calls into action classes, evaluates them against damage-control rules, path policies, and project policy, maps them to autonomy dispositions, and audits every decision to a daily-rotated NDJSON ledger.

pages.title: Domains scheduling
pages.summary: The scheduling domain owns three things: the session cost budget that scores spend against a ceiling, the fleet node registry that turns N machines into one pinnable capacity pool, and the local-capacity resolver that sizes worker concurrency under fleet.concurrency.

pages.title: Domains session
pages.summary: The session domain owns the persistence vocabulary (SessionEntry union), the lifecycle manager, context token accounting, the compaction pipeline, the task board store, and the pure validating continuity fold. It defines what a session is on disk and how a turn flows from append to durable replay.

pages.title: Vendored Tool Registry and Resolution
pages.summary: How Clio pins external terminal programs (herdr, yazi, croc), downloads and verifies them on request, and resolves them through a PATH-first ladder; including the dependency-free zip/tar.gz archive readers.

pages.title: Engine
pages.summary: The worker-subprocess engine boundary: the unified loop guard, the pi-agent worker runtime with its Claude SDK and external-CLI branches, per-provider request payload patches, the Claude tool-safety mediator, and the session JSONL ledger.

pages.title: Engine acp
pages.summary: Agent Client Protocol v1 server and delegation client for Clio, including the stdio JSON-RPC transport, permission mediation, headless command catalog, and ACP peer lifecycle.

pages.title: Engine apis
pages.summary: The engine's provider API layer: two registered providers (OpenAI-completions and Ollama-native), a shared capacity-aware residency reconciler for local runtimes, a degraded-inference watchdog, and per-runtime adapters for LM Studio, llama.cpp router, and Ollama.

pages.title: Entry point
pages.summary: The composition root that wires all domain bundles, resolves boot options, coordinates extension reloads, and activates the panes extension for interactive sessions.

pages.title: Interactive
pages.summary: The terminal user interface that hosts the chat loop, the streaming transcript, the status footer, the theme, and the export/view surfaces, and how events flow through its composition root.

pages.title: Interactive overlays
pages.summary: The TUI's modal and full-screen overlay panels — the shared list browser, the Library browser with its plan/review/apply lifecycle, the Settings Center, the model picker, the ask-user interview, and the session-tree navigator — and how they take keyboard ownership, enforce their boundaries, and release them.

pages.title: Interactive renderers
pages.summary: Pure functions that transform session data, tool results, and worker answers into terminal-styled text rows for the Clio TUI.

pages.title: Scripts
pages.summary: Checkout-only tooling under scripts/: the drift/lint gate, the library and skill pinning pipeline, the release qualification gate, the Pi API surface diff, and the two operator-run benches.

pages.title: Contract tests
pages.summary: The contract test suite that guards Clio's behavioral invariants, covering state isolation, dispatch routing, engine lifecycle, smoke tests of the built binary, ACP boundary behavior, and import-boundary enforcement.

pages.title: Tests extended
pages.summary: The tests/extended suite: how the full end-to-end behavior of the TUI, compaction lifecycle, library import/browser, dispatch board, configure wizard, and rendering invariants is exercised under pnpm run test:full, and the isolation harness they share.

pages.title: Tools
pages.summary: The tool system through which the model reads and mutates the world: registration, placement, lazy loading, observation reservation, and the individual tool implementations for context, gateway, code navigation, dispatch orchestration, monitoring, and script execution.

pages.title: Tools data
pages.summary: Streaming inspection, selection, and validation of CSV/TSV, JSON, and JSON Lines files, exposed through the `data` tool; every result carries honest view flags and typed refusals instead of guesses.

pages.title: Tools verify
pages.summary: The verify tool is a single EXECUTE entry point for declared verification: it lists package scripts, project catalog checks, and toolchain-derived checks, and runs one by exact id. It executes commands through safe-exec and attaches a three-part judgement (execution, validation, scientific validity) to every result.

pages.title: Worker runtime
pages.summary: The worker subprocess runtime: NDJSON protocol, spec contract, control-lane steering, attestation frames, and the boundary invariants that keep the bulk lane and control lane separated.

plan.overview: Clio Coder is a provider-agnostic coding-agent harness for terminal, headless, ACP, and GUI use, built on the Pi SDK. It provides typed tools for reading, editing, searching, and executing code, with a safety net that gates unfamiliar actions behind approval cards and records evidence of every run. The codebase is organized by domain: `src/domains/**` holds the business logic (dispatch, session, context, providers, safety, evidence, memory, etc.), `src/engine/**` isolates the Pi SDK boundary and model APIs, `src/interactive/**` builds the terminal UI, `src/tools/**` defines the typed tool surface, and `src/cli/**` is the command-line entry point. A newcomer should start with the domain pages: dispatch explains how work is delegated to workers, context explains how Clio indexes and adopts a repository, safety explains the autonomy model and protected paths, and the engine pages explain how model calls are routed through provider runtimes. The worker protocol (src/worker) and the composition root (src/entry) tie these domains together into a working harness.
